page: Microsoft Azure D96ns_v6 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dnv6 family, virtualized on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with an Intel processor configuration offering 96 dedicated vCPUs alongside 384 GB of memory, reflecting a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance provides no GPU accelerators, targeting non-graphical compute environments.

The instance is architected for network optimization and premium storage compatibility. It does not provide onboard local disk storage, operating entirely as a diskless compute node that relies on network-attached storage services for data persistence. This storage model allows organizations to adjust storage volume capacities and IOPS tiers independently from the compute envelope.

With a high allocation of dedicated compute resources and network-optimized connectivity, the D96ns_v6 is structured to support heavy parallel processing without local disk overhead. Appropriate production workloads include enterprise application backends, large relational and NoSQL database engines, distributed data processing, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and high-concurrency web services.
description: Microsoft Azure D96ns_v6 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine within the Dnv6 family, hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. Powered by an Intel processor platform, the instance features 96 dedicated vCPUs and 384 GB of total system memory, sustaining a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local disk storage or graphics acceleration hardware, requiring external network-attached premium storage for stateful deployments. Designed with network optimization in mind, the instance caters to enterprise architectures that require sustained virtual networking throughput and high-density multi-core compute. The resource balance makes the D96ns_v6 suitable for hosting high-throughput web service clusters, large database servers, distributed batch analytics, and resource-intensive enterprise application platforms.
